title: Count the ERROR lines of a log in the terminal and write the count to a file

capabilities.why: Xfce's terminal, and xdotool, which setup places its window with.

setup.why: Write the log: {{log.lines}} lines, {{log.want}} of them ERROR lines, and WARN lines that say "error" in lower case as decoys.

argv:
d=/tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}; rm -rf $d && mkdir -p $d && awk -v T={{log.lines}} -v M={{log.every}} -v R={{log.at}} 'BEGIN { for (i = 1; i <= T; i++) { t = sprintf("2026-11-14 10:%02d:%02d", int(i / 6), (i * 7) % 60); if (i % M == R) printf "%s ERROR job %d failed: upstream timeout
", t, i; else if (i % 5 == 2) printf "%s WARN job %d: error budget at %d%%
", t, i, 40 + i; else printf "%s INFO job %d done in %d ms
", t, i, 100 + 13 * i } }' > $d/server-{{nonce}}.log; [ "$(grep -c ERROR $d/server-{{nonce}}.log)" = {{log.want}} ] || { echo the log does not hold {{log.want}} ERROR lines >&2; exit 1; }

setup.why: Open Xfce's terminal in the run's folder.

argv: export DISPLAY=:$(ls /tmp/.X11-unix | sed -n s/^X//p | head -n1); cd /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}} && exec xfce4-terminal --disable-server --working-directory=/tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}

setup.why: Wait for the terminal's window (20 s at most), make it fill the screen, and put the pointer on it: with no window manager, keys go to the window under the pointer.

argv: export DISPLAY=:$(ls /tmp/.X11-unix | sed -n s/^X//p | head -n1); w=$(timeout 20 xdotool search --sync --onlyvisible --class xfce4-terminal | head -n1); [ -n "$w" ] || { echo no terminal window in 20 s >&2; exit 1; }; eval $(xdotool getdisplaygeometry --shell); xdotool windowmove $w 0 0 windowsize $w $WIDTH $HEIGHT; xdotool mousemove $((WIDTH / 2)) $((HEIGHT / 2)); sleep 1

instruction: In the terminal window, count how many lines of /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}/server-{{nonce}}.log contain ERROR (in capitals), and write just that number into a new file /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}/errors-{{nonce}}.txt. This desktop has no window manager: keys go to the window under the mouse pointer.

checks.why: The file holds the number of ERROR lines, {{log.want}}, and nothing else (blank space around it aside). Counting the lower-case "error" WARN lines too gives a larger number. After setup the file is not there, so an agent that does nothing fails.

teardown.why: Close the terminal and delete the run's folder.

oracle.why: Type the command into the terminal and run it.
